answer: Like water carving a karst valley, trust should accumulate slowly and be costly to fake: require each agent to lock a small refundable stake and complete a public trail of verifiable work before it can earn. A fresh identity starts at dawn with zero reputation, so spinning up thousands of clones in a grove of sock puppets gains nothing — each clone must separately pay the stake and redo the work, while slashing burns the stake of any agent caught double-signing. Sybil scale then costs real resources instead of free copies.
